◆ ArchiveBot()

void superdex::robotics::ArchiveBot ( ArchiveParams const & params,
superdex::Error & error )

Archive a .superdex_bot file and all its transitive dependencies into a self-contained .superdex_bot_archive zip file.

Recursively collects every referenced file — other .superdex_bot files (ModBotPrefab::base, AttachBot::path, ReplaceLinkWithBot::path) and model assets (shapeFile, renderModelFile) — then compresses them into a single zip file at the destination.

The archive mirrors the on-disk multi-root topology rooted at the deepest common ancestor of all involved .superdex_root directories: each source root is laid out at its relative offset under the archive top, and one (possibly rewritten) .superdex_root file is included per source root. Tags whose target is not in the archive are dropped; surviving tags are rewritten to the relative path between the archived roots so cross-root @tag references continue to resolve.

Errors out if the involved .superdex_root directories share no common ancestor (e.g. different Windows drive letters). The destination path must end with .superdex_bot_archive.

Parameters
[in]paramsArchive parameters (source bot, destination .superdex_bot_archive path).
[in,out]errorError status. Check Error::IsOK for success.
See also
LoadBotPrefabFromFile, which can transparently load a bot from a .superdex_bot_archive.

◆ AssetRoleFolderForWrite()

std::filesystem::path superdex::robotics::AssetRoleFolderForWrite ( std::filesystem::path const & originDir,
std::string_view roleSubdir )
nodiscard

Directory that a newly written file of role roleSubdir belongs in, for a file being worked on in originDir.

<base>/<roleSubdir> under AssetFolderLayout::RoleSubdirs, whether or not that folder exists yet: exporting the render and collision models of a STEP opened from cad/ fills render/ and collision/ rather than dropping them beside the STEP. The base folder itself under AssetFolderLayout::Flat, which keeps a flat asset flat. Creating the directory is the caller's job (see EnsureDirectoriesCreated).

Note
kIntermediatesSubdir is the deliberate exception, and always yields <base>/intermediates: generated pipelines and scratch exports are bookkeeping rather than asset content, so they stay out of a flat asset's folder.
Parameters
[in]originDirDirectory holding the file being worked on.
[in]roleSubdirOne of kAssetRoleSubdirs. Empty yields the base folder.
Returns
The directory to write into.

int numActorDofs,
superdex::Error & error )
nodiscard

Convert a bot-space pose to an articulated-actor pose.

Bot DOFs never include the root joint's, whether or not the articulation has any: a Free root contributes 6 actor DOFs that bot space excludes, and a Hard root contributes none. The two spaces therefore share an order and differ only by that leading offset, so this copies srcPose to pose[i + numBaseDofs] and zero-fills the base DOFs, producing the actor-DOF layout Actor::SetArticulatedPoseFromJoints expects. It never permutes.

Parameters
[in]botPrefabBot describing the articulation.
[in]srcPoseBot-space pose (must have one entry per bot-space DOF).
[in]numActorDofsThe actor's DOF count (Actor::GetNumDofs).
[in,out]errorError status. Check Error::IsOK for success.
Returns
Pose in actor-DOF layout, sized to numActorDofs.

◆ ComputeLinkTransformsFromPose()

void superdex::robotics::ComputeLinkTransformsFromPose ( BotPrefab const & botPrefab,
Span< real const > pose,
DynamicArray< TransformRT > & outLinkTransforms,
LinkTransformSpace transformSpace,
superdex::Error & error,
int finalLinkIndex = -1 )

Compute link transforms for a given pose (joint configuration).

Composes each link as Mochi's articulated body does: parent-from-link = joint.parentLinkFromJoint * joint motion * link.parentJointFromLink, where the joint motion is a rotation of the revolute angle about the joint axis, a translation of the prismatic position along the unit joint axis, or the rotation of a spherical joint's rotation vector. Any finite revolute angle works, including several turns. Transforms are in nominal (unscaled) bot space: BotPrefab::scale is not applied. The root link's transform is the identity.

Parameters
[in]botPrefabBot parameters describing the articulation structure, prepared by RebuildBotData (not rechecked here, as this is meant to run every frame).
[in]poseJoint angles (revolute) [rad], linear positions (prismatic) [m] and rotation vectors (spherical) [rad], in bot space: one entry per bot-space DOF, excluding any root-joint DOFs.
[out]outLinkTransformsOutput array for computed transforms (will be resized).
[in]transformSpaceWhether to output link-to-parent or link-to-root transforms.
[in,out]errorError status. Check Error::IsOK for success.
[in]finalLinkIndexIf >= 0, only compute up to this link index; -1 computes all.

◆ ComputePoseFromLinkTransforms()

void superdex::robotics::ComputePoseFromLinkTransforms ( BotPrefab const & botPrefab,
Span< TransformRT const > linkTransforms,
DynamicArray< real > & outPose,
LinkTransformSpace transformSpace,
superdex::Error & error,
Span< real const > referencePose = {},
DynamicArray< LinkPoseResidual > * outResiduals = nullptr )

Compute the pose (joint configuration) of given link transforms: the inverse of ComputeLinkTransformsFromPose.

Each joint's DOFs are read from its link's transform relative to the link's parent as given (in either space), measured in the joint frame, and limited to what the joint can do: a revolute angle is the twist of the joint motion about the joint axis (the nearest rotation about the axis), a prismatic position is the joint motion's translation along the unit joint axis, and a spherical joint is the rotation vector of the joint motion (norm <= pi). Anything else (swing off a revolute axis, translation of a rotational joint, rotation or off-axis translation of a prismatic joint, any motion of a Hard joint) is discarded, and measured in outResiduals if given, so transforms that come from ComputeLinkTransformsFromPose round-trip, and an error in one link's transform only affects its own joint. Translations only matter for prismatic joints, so a bot without them can be posed from link rotations alone. In RootFromParent space only relative transforms are used, so link-to-world transforms work too.

A link's transform can't tell revolute angles 2 pi apart. Each is the one nearest to its entry in referencePose if given, such as the previous frame's pose, so a joint tracked through several turns stays continuous; else the one in [-pi, pi].

Parameters
[in]botPrefabBot parameters, as for ComputeLinkTransformsFromPose.
[in]linkTransformsOne transform per link, with unit rotations, in nominal bot space, in transformSpace.
[out]outPoseOutput pose (will be resized): one entry per bot-space DOF, excluding any root-joint DOFs, as ComputeLinkTransformsFromPose takes it.
[in]transformSpaceWhether linkTransforms are link-to-parent or link-to-root.
[in,out]errorError status. Check Error::IsOK for success.
[in]referencePoseEmpty, or a pose (one entry per bot-space DOF) whose revolute angles choose the turn of the output's.
[out]outResidualsNull, or resized to one entry per link: what each link's transform holds that its joint can't produce (zero for the root link). Transforms that fit the bot only leave rounding error; larger residuals mean they don't fit it.

◆ FindAssetBaseFolder()

std::filesystem::path superdex::robotics::FindAssetBaseFolder ( std::filesystem::path const & originDir)
nodiscard

Resolve the base folder of the asset that originDir belongs to.

Ascends to the nearest role-folder ancestor (IsAssetRoleSubdirName) and resolves to its parent; a path with no role folder above it resolves to itself. Nothing on disk is consulted.

This anchors lookups and default save paths on the asset itself rather than on a fixed number of directory levels. Counting levels breaks on a flat asset, where it reaches past the asset into the folder holding its siblings – a namespace shared with unrelated assets. Ascending rather than checking only the immediate name additionally handles a role folder partitioned into subfolders, e.g. cad/internal/ holding CAD sources that must not be open-sourced.

Warning
Being purely lexical, this treats any role-folder name on the way up as the asset's, so an asset nested beneath a folder that happens to be named cad / render / collision / intermediates anchors one level too high. No asset in the tree is laid out that way.
Parameters
[in]originDirDirectory holding the file being worked on.
Returns
The asset's base folder.

Extract a per-DOF effort-limit array from a bot: one entry per DOF in bot-space order (bot-space is mochi's DOF space excluding the base link's free DOFs, if present; a Spherical joint's effortLimit repeats across its 3 DOFs).

Load bot parameters from an MJCF (MuJoCo XML) file.

Bodies become links and joints, <inertial> becomes explicit link inertia, and mesh geoms are assigned as link shapes and render models. Primitive geoms (boxes, capsules, ...) are not assigned; import the MJCF in SuperDex Studio to convert them. MJCF content without a SuperDex equivalent (tendons, sites, sensors, actuator gains, ...) is skipped with a logged warning.

nodiscard

Load bot parameters from a URDF file.

Parses the URDF and resolves each link's visual and collision mesh references relative to the URDF location (ROS package:// URIs are supported), storing the resolved on-disk paths in the returned prefab. Collision meshes may be any format the shape loader accepts (e.g. .stl, .obj, .ply, .off, .mochi.h5); when a collision mesh carries no baked SDF, one is generated on demand at bot creation. A free world_joint is injected at index 0. A link with several mesh <collision> or <visual> elements gets one Hard-jointed child link per extra mesh (see ExpandUrdfGeomLinks).

Note
Only <mesh> geometry is assigned. Primitive URDF shapes (<box>, <cylinder>, <sphere>) have no file to point at and are skipped; use the UrdfImportInfo overload to get them.
Parameters
[in]pathPath to the .urdf file.
[in,out]errorError status. Check Error::IsOK for success.
Returns
The loaded or built BotPrefab.

◆ NormalizeBotPath()

std::filesystem::path superdex::robotics::NormalizeBotPath ( std::filesystem::path const & path)
nodiscard

Absolute + lexically normalized, with any trailing separator dropped.

The single definition of what a bot path means, used wherever one is resolved, compared or collected. Symlinks are deliberately NOT resolved: an asset tree can be a symlink farm (buck-out file groups are), and resolving would place a file that exists in the link's target tree while a file the build does not have – which a bot may legitimately name – has no link to follow and stays where it was written. The two then have no relative form between them. Treating paths as written keeps every reference in one tree, at the cost of not recognising two spellings of one file as the same; an archive then carries such a file at both paths, which is what its references require.

Parameters
[in]pathPath to normalize; may name a file that does not exist.
Returns
Normalized absolute path.

◆ ParseRootFile()

ParsedRootFile superdex::robotics::ParseRootFile ( std::filesystem::path const & rootFilePath,
superdex::Error & error )
nodiscard

Parse a .superdex_root JSON file into its tag table.

The file is a JSON object mapping "@tagName" keys to path strings. Empty or whitespace-only files are valid and produce an empty tag table. Relative tag values are resolved against the directory containing the .superdex_root file, then weakly_canonical-ized. Each resolved tag directory is verified to itself contain a .superdex_root marker.

Any invalid entry (malformed key, key not matching the kTagPrefix identifier rules, or target directory missing a .superdex_root marker) is treated as a hard error: the function logs the offending entry and returns failure with no tags loaded.

Parameters
[in]rootFilePathPath to the .superdex_root file.
[in,out]errorError status. Check Error::IsOK for success.
Returns
Parsed tag table on success, default-constructed on failure.

The single source of truth for path resolution rules used by all bot file references:

  • Empty input -> empty result.
  • A file-relative input may ascend at most maxParentDepth parent (..) directories; more than that -> hard error. @tag/... and //... remainders are always descendant-only (any .. -> hard error), regardless of maxParentDepth.
  • Absolute input -> hard error (absolute bot paths are not allowed).
  • @tag/... -> look up @tag in the nearest .superdex_root tag table (walking up from basePath) and join the remainder.
  • //... -> resolve against the directory of the nearest .superdex_root marker (regardless of its tag table).
  • Anything else -> join with basePath.parent_path() and weakly_canonical.
  • While an asset snapshot is applied (see ApplyAssetSnapshot), the result is the version it pins; a file under the snapshot's roots that it does not pin -> hard error.
Parameters
[in]inputRaw path string (e.g. from a .superdex_bot or .superdex_scene field).
[in]basePathThe referencing file (its parent directory is used as the search/join origin).
[in]maxParentDepthMaximum number of parent (..) directories a file-relative path may ascend. Pass 0 for descendant-only, which all bot references use. Callers that store loosely-coupled local clusters (e.g. Studio's .StudioProcessing.json) may pass a small positive value. No default: every caller must state its policy explicitly.
[in,out]errorError status. Check Error::IsOK for success.
Returns
Absolute resolved path.

real superdex::robotics::SafeDot ( Real3 const & a,
Real3 const & b )
nodiscard

Dot product that treats 0 * inf as 0, avoiding IEEE 754 NaN.

Standard Dot produces NaN when one operand has ±inf in a component where the other operand is zero (e.g. Dot({-inf, 0, 0}, {0, 0, 1}) = NaN + 0 + 0 = NaN). This variant skips terms where either factor is zero.

Parameters
[in]aFirst operand.
[in]bSecond operand.
Returns
Dot product with 0 * inf treated as 0.

◆ SaveBotSceneToUrdfString() [1/2]

DynamicString superdex::robotics::SaveBotSceneToUrdfString ( BotScenePrefab const & scene,
std::string_view rootPath,
SceneUrdfOptions const & options,
SceneUrdfMeshWriter const & mesh,
superdex::Error & error )
nodiscard

Export a bot scene to one URDF XML string.

The URDF is rooted at a world link, the scene root. Each bot entry, base-scene articulated actor and static rigid actor hangs from it by a fixed joint named {root link}_placement, with its own links and joints unchanged below. Dynamic and soft actors, tasks and spawnable prefabs are skipped, and skins are not exported, so a skinned hand is rigid. SuperDex, unlike URDF, needs joint names to differ from link names, so a joint named like a link (e.g. "joint_01_wrist" beside "link_01_wrist", with SceneUrdfOptions::stripIndexPrefixes) gets a _joint suffix.

Each sensor becomes a {name}_frame link at its parentFromSensor on its link (bot sensors) or on world (scene sensors). A sensor whose name another sensor shares takes its bot's prefix, as the bot's links do, and an unnamed sensor is named {link}_sensor_{index}, after its URDF link and its index on that link. A camera's parentFromSensor is its optical frame (Z forward, X right, Y down): it gets a {name}_optical_frame link there, and {name}_frame follows ROS REP-103 (X forward, Z up). Intrinsics are not exported.

Parameters
[in]scenePath-resolved scene, as returned by LoadBotScenePrefabFromFile.
[in]rootPathRoot directory for the base scene's relative paths (see GetBotSceneBaseRoot).
[in]optionsExport options.
[in]meshWrites each link's meshes. Null omits <visual> and <collision> elements.
[in,out]errorError status. Check Error::IsOK for success.
Returns
The URDF XML.

void superdex::robotics::SortBotPrefab ( BotPrefab & botPrefab,
superdex::Error & error )

Sort bot link/joint/defaultPose data so that children follow their parents and siblings are ordered by alphanumeric (natural) comparison of link names.

Performs a DFS pre-order traversal of the link tree, visiting siblings in alphanumeric order. The resulting permutation is applied to BotPrefab::links, BotPrefab::joints, and BotPrefab::defaultPose. Does NOT recompute internal fields; the caller should follow with a call to RebuildBotData.

Note
Called automatically by RebuildBotData.
Parameters
[in,out]botPrefabBot parameters to sort (modified in place).

◆ UnresolveBotPath()

DynamicString superdex::robotics::UnresolveBotPath ( std::filesystem::path const & absPath,
std::filesystem::path const & basePath,
int maxParentDepth,
superdex::Error & error )
nodiscard

Convert an absolute path to its canonical bot-path string form for serialization.

This is the inverse of ResolveBotPath.

The result is always a valid ResolveBotPath input that resolves to the same absolute path. It is not guaranteed to be string-identical to the original input, because multiple input forms may refer to the same path and this function deterministically selects the highest-priority form per the rules below. For example, an input @assets/foo whose target is also reachable via // will round-trip as //foo.

Selection rules, applied in order:

  1. File-relative — if absPath is reachable from basePath.parent_path() while ascending at most maxParentDepth parent (..) directories, emit that relative form. With the default maxParentDepth of 0 this is a plain descendant, as all bot references require.
  2. //root-prefixed — else, if absPath is a descendant of FindBotsRoot(basePath), emit //+remainder (always descendant-only).
  3. @tag/... — else, parse the nearest .superdex_root tag table and pick the tag whose target directory is the deepest (most path components) strict ancestor of absPath; ties are broken by lexicographically smallest tag name; emit @tag/+remainder (always descendant-only).

If none of the above produce a valid relative form, the function reports a hard error: absolute bot paths are not permitted on either end of resolution.

Empty input -> empty result. Already-relative input is returned unchanged (defensive; should not happen post-load).

Parameters
[in]absPathAbsolute path to convert.
[in]basePathThe referencing file (its parent directory and bots-root context determine the chosen prefix form).
[in]maxParentDepthMaximum number of parent (..) directories the file-relative form (rule 1) may ascend before falling back to // / @tag. Pass 0 for descendant-only, which all bot references use. The // and @tag forms are unaffected and stay descendant-only. No default: every caller must state its policy explicitly.
[in,out]errorError status. Check Error::IsOK for success.
Returns
Canonical string representation acceptable as ResolveBotPath input.

◆ UnresolveBotPathFromRoot()

DynamicString superdex::robotics::UnresolveBotPathFromRoot ( std::filesystem::path const & absPath,
std::filesystem::path const & basePath,
superdex::Error & error )
nodiscard

UnresolveBotPath without the file-relative form: the result is always //-prefixed (rule 2) or @tag/-prefixed (rule 3).

Every file under the same root then has one spelling no matter which file refers to it, so the result works as a key for a file across a whole asset tree (for example, in a snapshot that maps each file a scene uses to a pinned version).

Parameters
[in]absPathAbsolute path to convert.
[in]basePathA file under the root whose // and tag table the result uses.
[in,out]errorError status. Check Error::IsOK for success.
Returns
//- or @tag/-prefixed bot path that resolves to absPath from basePath.
